items.title: Dave McKenna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Ray Santisi, a fellow piano players from Boston called it, “Mammaries from cats.”

ctx.x: Did you ever get a request that you wouldn’t play because —

No, if I know it I play it. Even a terrible song. But try to dismiss it quickly, and play it through and play one and a half choruses. But I’m embarrassed because there are some tunes that I’m prejudiced against, that I never liked, and I should have learned, and I have mental blocks about them. “New York New York.” When I was at the Copley that was big, and I had said, “Well if you really want to hear it I’ve got the music upstairs.” Once they said, “Why don’t you?” Jesus, I went upstairs in my room and got it,…
